key_takeaways: Australia does not issue a marriage licence, and the Notice of Intended Marriage (NOIM) is not 'valid for 18 months': you give it at least one month and no more than 18 months before the wedding, counted back from your date.
If your wedding moves to a date more than 18 months after you gave notice, ask your celebrant whether you need a new NOIM; if only the celebrant changes, the NOIM can be transferred.
Your celebrant has 14 days to send your paperwork to the state or territory registry, and the official registry certificate has no published expiry date.

DFAT prints no expiry on a CNI or an apostille, but destinations set their own limits: about three months for a CNI in Bali, 90 days for a CNI in France (where one partner must be a French citizen or legal resident), six months for Italy's Atto Notorio and for a licence issued in Greece.
Order time-limited documents last, once the deciding authority has told you exactly what it wants, and confirm every limit with that authority for your own passports.

faq.q: How long is a NOIM valid in Australia?
faq.a: It has no validity period as such. You give it at least one month and no more than 18 months before the wedding, counted back from your date.
No official source we checked gives a registry marriage certificate an expiry date, though some overseas authorities want recently issued copies.

faq.q: What happens if we postpone our wedding after giving our NOIM?
faq.a: If the new date falls more than 18 months after you gave notice, ask your celebrant whether you need a new NOIM, and recheck any overseas documents.

faq.q: What is the best proof of marriage in Australia?
faq.a: The official certificate from the registry in the state or territory where you married, not the ceremonial one from the day.

faq.q: How long is a marriage licence valid overseas?
faq.a: A marriage licence issued in Greece is valid for six months (couples marrying from abroad may use a home-country document instead). Elsewhere the limit often sits on supporting documents.

faq.q: Does a Certificate of No Impediment (CNI) expire?
faq.a: DFAT publishes no validity period; the destination decides. Bali's registries normally refuse one over three months old, and France (where one partner must be a French citizen or legal resident) gives it 90 days.
